title: Sable and the Uniform
premise: In 1890s river-port Sablemouth, Ansel Kavanagh—pearl diver's child, indentured to the Harrow & Vane Trading Company—has survived by being unremarkable. When an infant is abandoned at the company door with a note reading 'forget this face,' Ansel recognizes the child as heir to a fortune the company's directors intend to erase, along with anyone who remembers it. Armed with a ledger page proving the inheritance and guided by a disgraced constable's uniform that grants passage where papers cannot, Ansel must move the evidence past three checkpoints before spring ice breaks the river and destroys the proof hidden beneath it. The story ends with Ansel surrendering their own name to the record in exchange for the child's future, choosing visibility over survival.
about_author: Felix Delacroix is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing shipping ledgers from forgotten river towns. Their fiction excavates the lives of people history recorded only as line items.

chapters.title: The Weight of Water
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. We meet them hauling cargo at Harrow & Vane's wharf, invisible by design, haunted by their drowned pearl-diver mother. A near-drowning of a coworker reveals Ansel can hold breath longer than any diver should. Emotional beat: quiet grief and self-erasure established.

chapters.title: A Bundle at the Door
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. During a February storm, an infant is left at the company door with a note: 'forget this face.' Director Vane orders the child sent to the workhouse by morning. Ansel, holding the baby, sees a birthmark matching one on a dead heiress they once glimpsed. Beat: reluctant awakening.

chapters.title: Ledger Lines
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, night infiltration of the counting house. They find a ledger page recording the child's true parentage—and a second entry authorizing its 'disposition.' Ansel steals the page. Beat: crossing the point of no return; fear sharpening into purpose.

chapters.title: The Uniform in the Attic
chapters.summary: Ansel seeks help from Odile Brannock, a laundress who mends for the constabulary. She reveals her brother's old constable's uniform, kept since his disgrace, and warns that wearing it is hanging offense territory. Beat: alliance formed; stakes named aloud.

chapters.title: Three Checkpoints
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. She maps the route downriver: the Tollgate, the Company Wharf inspection, and the Icehouse Bridge, each requiring different papers or faces. The ice will break within weeks, flooding the low archive where corroborating records sit. Beat: plan crystallizes; clock starts.

chapters.title: What the Child Remembers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Caring for the baby ('Sable,' named for the river), Ansel confronts their own erased childhood—the name taken when they were indentured at six. Flashbacks to the pearl beds. Beat: identity theme deepens; tenderness becomes resolve.

chapters.title: Vane's Quiet Men
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Two company enforcers begin asking about 'a missing bundle.' Ansel's bunk is searched; they barely hide the ledger page in a coil of rope. Beat: hunted feeling begins; paranoia replaces routine.

chapters.title: The Constable Who Wasn't
chapters.summary: Ansel wears the uniform for the first time, walking through the Tollgate district and discovering how differently the world treats a badge. They extract a copy of a death certificate from a sympathetic clerk. Beat: intoxication and shame of borrowed authority.

chapters.title: Old Debts
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Her brother Callum, the disgraced constable, resurfaces drunk and bitter. He recognizes the uniform's absence from his trunk and forces his way into the plot—as liability or ally, unclear. Beat: complication; trust tested.

chapters.title: Checkpoint One: The Tollgate
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. First smuggling run: the ledger page sewn into the uniform lining, carried past the Tollgate during a grain shipment. A sharp-eyed sergeant nearly unmasks Ansel; Callum's knowledge of procedure saves them. Beat: first victory, narrowly bought.

chapters.title: The Price of a Name
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Vane offers Ansel freedom papers if they hand over 'the foundling's effects.' The offer tempts: legal personhood, the thing Ansel has never had. Beat: moral crux; temptation given real weight.

chapters.title: Icehouse Bridge
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. Reconnaissance of the third checkpoint reveals the bridge guarded after a theft, and the flood archive already being drained early. The timeline collapses from weeks to days. Beat: dread; plan fraying.

chapters.title: Callum's Confession
chapters.summary: Callum's POV. He admits he was dismissed for refusing to falsify a drowning report—one connected to the heiress's death. His testimony could corroborate the ledger. Beat: redemption offered; the past re-entering the present.

chapters.title: Betrayal at the Wharf
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Callum, desperate for reinstatement, sells word of the route to Vane's men. Checkpoint Two becomes a trap; Ansel escapes by diving into the freezing river, the evidence lost—or so the pursuers believe. Beat: betrayal, near-death, apparent ruin.

chapters.title: Breath Like Mother's
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Clinging to a piling, Ansel survives underwater using the pearl-diver's breath rhythm their mother taught them, retrieving the oilskin-wrapped page from the riverbed. Beat: inheritance reclaimed—not money, but skill and memory.

chapters.title: The Workhouse Ledger
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. With checkpoints compromised, Odile proposes the unthinkable: enter the flooded archive before the ice breaks, using Callum's genuine warrant—reinstated by a magistrate Odile has blackmailed with laundry-room secrets. Beat: desperate ingenuity; uneasy truce with Callum.

chapters.title: Under the River Ice
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. The archive dive: Ansel descends through broken ice into the drowned record room, recovering the corroborating registry as the structure groans apart. Nearly trapped, they surface changed. Beat: climax of endurance; fear transmuted into certainty.

chapters.title: Checkpoint Three: Icehouse Bridge
chapters.summary: Ensemble POV shifts. The final run: Ansel in uniform, Odile driving a hearse wagon, Callum flashing his warrant—all three documents converge at the last checkpoint just as Vane arrives to stop them. Beat: climax; every thread pulled taut.

chapters.title: The Face That Must Be Remembered
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. Confrontation with Vane on the breaking ice. Ansel chooses not to flee but to stand and be seen, declaring their own stolen name and the child's true one before witnesses. Vane's men waver; the ice cracks. Beat: moral climax; invisibility renounced.

chapters.title: After the Break
chapters.summary: Odile's POV. The river breaks; the archive floods, but the evidence is already in a magistrate's hands. Vane arrested; Callum testifies and loses his career again, willingly. Beat: justice outside the law vindicated at cost.

chapters.title: Papers
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV. In court, Ansel signs their full recovered name—Kavanagh restored—surrendering anonymity forever to secure Sable's guardianship under Odile. Beat: bittersweet triumph; identity chosen, not assigned.

chapters.title: Sable and the Uniform
chapters.summary: Ansel's POV, epilogue. A year later: Ansel runs messages in a plain coat, the uniform hung in Odile's attic as a relic. Sable, toddling on the wharf, points at the river without fear. Beat: resolution; the river gives as well as takes.
